resumen: ## How we affect the environment
Everything we do affects our **environment**. Our food, water and even the air we breathe come from it. People who drop **litter** or make unnecessary **noise** harm the environment.
## Natural resources

Everything we use is made from **natural resources**: air, water, coal, oil, natural gas, rocks and soil, animals and plants. Power stations use them to make electricity, but they also **pollute** (dirty) the air.
## Non-renewable resources
- **Coal, oil, natural gas and metal ores** can only be used once. We cannot make any more after we have used them up.
- They are like a jar of sweets: use them carefully and they last for many years; waste them and they are gone forever.
## Renewable resources
- **Animals, trees and other plants** can be replaced: new ones grow in their place.
- **Sunlight, wind, waves, tides and fast-flowing rivers** will always be there to make more electricity.

resumen: ## Rubbish and litter
- **Rubbish** is anything we do not want or need.
- **Litter** is any rubbish we do not put in a bin or recycle.
## Landfill sites
Much of our rubbish goes into holes in the ground called **landfill sites** (often old stone quarries or sand and gravel pits).
- Birds, flies and **rats** feed on the rubbish and spread **germs**.
- They produce poisonous gases such as **methane** and **carbon dioxide**, which add to **global warming**.
- Apple cores, vegetable peelings and paper **rot away** quickly, but most rubbish never rots.
## Making less rubbish
Choose things with little **packaging**, **reuse** plastic bags or use strong cloth bags.
## Why is litter dangerous?

It is dirty, looks nasty and carries **germs**. Cigarette ends, matches and broken glass in the sun can start **fires**. It harms animals: glass cuts feet, cans cut mouths, six-pack rings trap small animals and plastic bags choke big animals.
Never pick up litter without wearing **gloves**.

resumen: ## Why recycle?

The world's **population** is growing quickly, so we make more rubbish. Throwing things away causes **pollution** and wastes valuable materials. **Recycling** and **reusing** is much better, but we only recycle a fraction of our rubbish.
## A family's dustbin (by weight)
Paper **30%** · Kitchen rubbish **23%** · Glass 10% · Dust 10% · Other 10% · Metals 9% · Plastics 5% · Cloth 3%.
## What can be recycled?
- **Glass**: recycled over and over again; it saves energy and raw materials. Even better to **reuse** jars and bottles. A recycled glass bottle uses only **one tenth** of the energy.
- **Plastics**: bottles are made into **fleece jackets** or **traffic cones**; bags and containers can be reused.
- **Clothing and textiles**: reused or made into mattress fillings, cloths, blankets and carpets.
- **Plant material**: fruit and vegetable waste makes **compost**, a natural **fertiliser**.
- **Metals**: drinks cans are **aluminium**. Recycling it uses only **one twentieth** of the energy and makes one twentieth of the pollution. Food cans are **steel** with a thin coating of **tin**.
- **Paper**: almost **one third** of our rubbish. It becomes toilet rolls, egg boxes and new paper. Each tonne recycled saves almost **15 trees**.

resumen: ## How is oil formed?
**Crude oil** formed from tiny plants and animals that lived in the sea **millions of years ago**. They died, sank, were buried by mud and sand and slowly changed into oil.
## Drilling for oil

Oil is found in layers deep underground, with **natural gas** in a layer above it. Workers drill **thousands of metres** through rock. Under the sea they drill from huge platforms called **oil rigs**; one rig can control several **wells**.
The deepest oil well (2009, Gulf of Mexico) was **10.7 km** deep.
## Uses of oil
Crude oil is made into **petrol, diesel, paraffin (kerosene), heating oil and asphalt**, and into **paints, detergents, plastics, synthetic rubber and pesticides**. Natural gas is used as a **fuel**.
## Problems with oil

Oil is pumped through pipes to a **port**, then carried by **oil tankers**. If a tanker runs aground or crashes, oil **spills**: sea plants, fish and shellfish die and **seabirds** with oil on their feathers cannot survive.
In April **2010** an oil rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing 11 people.
Oil is **non-renewable**: we must not waste it and must find energy that does not harm the environment.

resumen: ## Energy
Everything we use or buy has been made using **energy**. Vehicles that move goods and people use energy, and flicking a switch uses energy as **electricity**.
## Fossil fuels

**Coal, oil and natural gas** are **fossil fuels**: they formed in the Earth from the remains of plants and animals that lived long ago. Most electricity comes from burning them; some comes from **wind, moving water or the Sun**.
Taking them out of the Earth damages the environment: digging coal leaves **large holes and heaps of waste**.
## Acid rain and smog
- Burning fossil fuels makes harmful gases. Some mix with water in clouds and make **acid rain** (acid like vinegar). It kills trees, plants and water animals and damages buildings.
- Warm sunshine can turn these gases into a murky brown layer called **smog**. It hurts eyes and damages lungs. In December **1952** a smog in **London** killed more than **4000** people.
## Global warming

Gases in the **atmosphere** trap some of the Sun's heat. Burning fossil fuels traps more, so the Earth warms up: **global warming**. Polar ice may melt (flooding low-lying countries), with more **droughts** and floods.
## Saving energy
- Travel: small cars use less fuel; **trains, trams and buses** use less energy per person; **walk or cycle** short journeys.

- At home: turn off lights and TVs, shut doors and windows when the heating is on, wear an extra jumper, have a **shower rather than a bath**, heat only the water you need, no air conditioning with windows open.

resumen: ## What is noise?
**Noise** is sound that we do not like or do not want. Like litter, noise is a kind of **pollution**: it spoils our environment.
## What causes noise?
Large **towns and cities** are very noisy. Even in the **countryside** there is noise from **aircraft, road traffic and farm machines**.
## How is noise harmful?
Your body **grows and repairs itself** when you are asleep, but it is hard to rest, sleep, think or work when it is noisy. Very loud noises can **damage your ears** and reduce your **hearing**.
The **Saturn V** space rocket made one of the loudest noises ever produced by people.
## How can we reduce noise?
- Cars, motorbikes and trucks have **silencers** to make engines quieter.
- **Curtains and carpets** absorb sound in large empty rooms with hard floors.
- **Soft foam or fibreglass** in the hollows in walls.
- **Double-glazed** or **triple-glazed** windows keep out noise.
- People in noisy places wear **ear defenders**.

resumen: ## Sharing ideas
To improve the environment, people get together and **share ideas**, then discuss which are **most important** and which can be done **easily**.
## Improving your school
- Design and make **litter bins** people enjoy using.
- **Plant trees** or make **window boxes** and **flower beds**. Planting makes the environment pleasant and can provide **food**.
- No garden? Plant flowers in **tubs** of soil or compost, or make **miniature gardens** in old **oil drums** or **car tyres** (recycled containers).
- **Colourful paintings** can make ugly walls look better.
## Encouraging wildlife
Make **nest boxes** for birds and **bats**, a **bird table** with fruit or seeds, a **bird bath** with fresh water every day, and plant flowers that **butterflies** like.
## Outside your school
To brighten up the streets, discuss your ideas with the **people in charge of the local roads**.
